passages.title: The first census
passages.summary: God commands a census of men eligible for war. Tribal leaders assist Moses and Aaron. Levites receive separate duties. The account presents a community organized for travel and service. Its totals are textual claims, not independently verified population counts.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how preparation can serve a community without reducing people to their assigned roles.

passages.title: The camp arranged
passages.summary: The tribes camp around the meeting tent in four groups. Their marching order follows the same arrangement. The sanctuary stands at the center of the camp. The ordering gives each group a place and a duty.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider what your daily arrangements show about your priorities.

passages.title: Levites and firstborn
passages.summary: The chapter names Aaron’s sons and assigns duties to the Levite families. Levites stand in place of Israel’s firstborn. Priestly work and other Levite service remain distinct. The account connects these duties with the rescue of the firstborn.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church manual connects redemption of the firstborn with deliverance. Keep that interpretation distinct from the census figures.

passages.title: Duties for moving the sanctuary
passages.summary: Moses and Aaron count Levites assigned to service. Kohath, Gershon, and Merari have different transport duties. Shared service requires clear duties. The sacred objects receive protection during travel.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how careful preparation can help others carry their responsibilities.

passages.title: Camp, restitution, and jealousy
passages.summary: The laws address exclusion from the camp, restitution for wrongs, and a ritual for a husband’s accusation against his wife. The ritual belongs to an unequal ancient legal system. Read its words carefully before connecting it with modern medical or legal claims.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the difference between accusation and proof. Do not use this ancient ritual as present-day guidance.

passages.title: Nazirite vows and blessing
passages.summary: The law describes a special vow, including limits on wine, hair cutting, and contact with the dead. Priests receive words of blessing. The vow marks a period of dedication. The priestly blessing asks for protection, favor, and peace.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a commitment can shape daily conduct. Read the blessing as a prayer for God’s care.

passages.title: Gifts from the tribal leaders
passages.summary: Tribal leaders bring wagons, oxen, and offerings for the sanctuary. Each leader’s altar gift receives a separate account. The repeated gifts give each tribe a place in the dedication. The transport gifts support different Levite duties.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how material gifts and practical support can make shared worship possible.

passages.title: Levites prepared for service
passages.summary: Aaron tends the lamps. The Levites undergo cleansing and appointment before beginning their service. Preparation concerns the community as well as the workers. The chapter also distinguishes ages for active duty and assistance.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how preparation and support can help people serve at different stages of life.

passages.title: Passover and the guiding cloud
passages.summary: Israel keeps Passover at Sinai. People unable to observe it at the first time receive another date. The cloud directs camp movements. The instructions address a real problem within the community. The cloud gives a shared signal for travel and rest.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how faithful observance can include people whose circumstances require accommodation.

passages.title: Departure from Sinai
passages.summary: God gives instructions for silver trumpets. Israel leaves Sinai. Moses invites Hobab to help guide the journey. Signals and local knowledge both support the journey. The account brings the organized camp into movement.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how shared signals and practical experience can help a group act together.

passages.title: Complaints, elders, and quail
passages.summary: The people complain about food. Moses asks for help. Seventy elders receive the Spirit, including Eldad and Medad in the camp. Moses accepts help and welcomes others’ prophetic gifts. The desire for meat also leads to judgment in the narrative.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies gratitude and meekness here. Consider Moses’s response to Eldad and Medad.

passages.title: Miriam and Aaron challenge Moses
passages.summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses. God defends Moses’s special role. Miriam becomes afflicted, and Moses prays for her. The account joins disputed authority with concern for a family member. The camp waits while Miriam remains outside it.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies respect for prophetic service. Read that theme alongside Moses’s prayer for Miriam.

passages.title: The spies report on Canaan
passages.summary: Moses sends twelve men to inspect Canaan. They return with fruit and reports of strong settlements. Caleb urges action. The same observations produce different judgments. The account distinguishes what the scouts see from what they conclude.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies Caleb’s faith. Consider how fear affects your use of available evidence.

passages.title: The people refuse to enter
passages.summary: The people want to return to Egypt. Joshua and Caleb urge trust. Moses intercedes, and the generation receives a judgment of wandering. The story gives consequences to a community decision. A later attack fails after the people reject the warning to remain.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects this account with hope through faith. Consider the duties that accompany trust.

passages.title: Offerings and reminders
passages.summary: The laws describe offerings after entry into the land. They address unintentional error, deliberate defiance, a Sabbath case, and garment fringes. The chapter places future worship beside present failures. Visible reminders help connect ordinary life with covenant duties.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider what reminders help you keep commitments. Keep the ancient civil punishment distinct from present practice.

passages.title: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram rebel
passages.summary: Korah and other leaders challenge Moses and Aaron. The account describes severe judgment and a later plague. Aaron makes atonement for the people. The chapter concerns authority, rivalry, and communal danger. Moses and Aaron also act to protect the congregation.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The manual studies priestly authority. Read the entire account, including the leaders’ concern for people facing judgment.

passages.title: Aaron’s staff buds
passages.summary: Each tribal leader supplies a staff. Aaron’s staff produces buds, flowers, and almonds. It remains as a sign at the sanctuary. The sign settles the dispute within the narrative. It does not provide external evidence for the event.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how the account links authority with the end of destructive rivalry.

passages.title: Priestly duties and support
passages.summary: God assigns duties to Aaron, his sons, and the Levites. Offerings and tithes support their service. The chapter joins sacred work with material provision. It also places duties and limits on those who receive support.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the responsibilities that accompany community support for religious service.

passages.title: The red heifer and cleansing
passages.summary: The law describes ashes from a red heifer and water used after contact with the dead. Eleazar has a role in preparing the rite. Contact with death changes ritual status. Ritual impurity must remain distinct from personal moral guilt.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the difference between ritual status and wrongdoing. Avoid treating bereavement as evidence of moral failure.

passages.title: Miriam dies, water flows, and Aaron dies
passages.summary: Miriam dies at Kadesh. Moses strikes the rock during a dispute over water. Edom refuses passage. Aaron dies after Eleazar receives his garments. The chapter records loss and leadership transition. Moses and Aaron also receive a judgment about entry into the land.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies meekness and trust. Read leadership duties alongside grief and the account’s limits on authority.

passages.title: The bronze serpent and eastern victories
passages.summary: The people suffer snakebites and receive a bronze serpent as a sign for healing. Israel then defeats Sihon and Og. The narrative combines complaint, healing, journeys, and war. Its victories do not establish a precise army route.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects the serpent with looking to Christ. Compare Alma 33 and Helaman 8.

passages.title: Balak sends for Balaam
passages.summary: Balak asks Balaam to curse Israel. During Balaam’s journey, his donkey sees an angel before he does. Balaam must speak the words God gives. The story questions the seer’s perception. The donkey recognizes the obstruction that Balaam initially misses.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies pressure to act against God’s will. Keep later comments about Balaam distinct from this chapter’s sequence.

passages.title: Balaam blesses Israel
passages.summary: Balak builds altars and seeks a curse. Balaam instead pronounces blessings. They move to another vantage point, but the result remains a blessing. A king cannot purchase the desired divine answer. The repeated attempts expose the limits of Balak’s control.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the pressure to give an answer that a powerful person wants to hear.

passages.title: A star and a scepter
passages.summary: Balaam gives further oracles about Israel and neighboring peoples. Balak dismisses him after the blessings continue. The poems describe rule and future conflict through images of a star and scepter. Later interpreters read these images in different ways.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the star and scepter with Christ. Identify that connection as an LDS interpretation.

passages.title: Peor and Phinehas
passages.summary: Israel joins worship at Peor. Phinehas kills Zimri and Cozbi during the crisis. The account describes the end of a plague. The story links worship, communal danger, and priestly zeal. Its violence requires historical context and cannot authorize present violence.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Read the manual’s priesthood discussion with care. Keep ancient narrative violence distinct from present religious duties.

passages.title: The second census
passages.summary: Moses and Eleazar count the next generation. The families receive lists, and inheritance depends on group size. Joshua and Caleb survive from the earlier census. The census prepares for land allocation. Its numbers remain claims within the text, not an independent population survey.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how continuity and change affect a community preparing for a new stage.

passages.title: The daughters’ petition and Joshua’s appointment
passages.summary: Zelophehad’s daughters ask for an inheritance because their father had no sons. God accepts their claim. Moses appoints Joshua before the congregation. A petition leads to a legal instruction. Leadership also passes through a public appointment rather than a private assumption.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how careful listening can reveal a gap in existing rules. The manual also studies Joshua’s appointment.

passages.title: Daily, Sabbath, and festival offerings
passages.summary: The laws list offerings for each day, Sabbaths, new moons, Passover, and the feast of first produce. The calendar gives worship a regular pattern. The chapter specifies what the community must supply.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how repeated acts can sustain remembrance and gratitude.

passages.title: Offerings in the seventh month
passages.summary: The law gives offerings for the trumpet day, the Day of Atonement, and the feast of booths. A changing pattern of offerings marks the festival days. The text joins sacred time with shared material commitments.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a calendar can help a community remember its duties together.

passages.title: Vows and household authority
passages.summary: The laws regulate vows. Fathers and husbands can cancel certain vows made by women under the stated conditions. The rules reflect unequal household authority in the ancient system. A vow also carries a serious expectation of fulfillment.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the responsibility of making promises. Do not transfer the ancient household rules directly into present relationships.

passages.title: War against Midian
passages.summary: Israel attacks Midian, and Balaam dies. Moses gives severe instructions about captives. The chapter also divides spoils and describes cleansing. The account includes violence against children and women. Its stated religious setting does not remove the need to examine that harm.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Read the entire chapter, including its violence. Keep this ancient war account distinct from present Church conduct.

passages.title: Eastern tribes make a promise
passages.summary: Reuben and Gad request land east of the Jordan. Moses requires their fighting men to assist the other tribes. Families can remain in the eastern settlements. The agreement joins a local request with shared responsibility. Land preference does not cancel the duty to support other tribes.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a personal or group benefit can carry obligations to the wider community.

passages.title: The journey remembered
passages.summary: The chapter lists camps from Egypt to the plains of Moab. It then gives instructions for entry into Canaan. The list preserves a narrative itinerary. Many camp identifications remain uncertain, so the map cannot show every stop as a verified point.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a community records its journey. Distinguish named camps from places whose locations are secure.

passages.title: Borders and appointed leaders
passages.summary: God describes the land’s boundaries and names leaders to divide it. Eleazar and Joshua receive leading roles. The boundaries concern an anticipated allocation. A description in the text is not proof that the community controlled every named border.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how clear duties can support a shared allocation. Keep expected borders distinct from verified historical control.

passages.title: Levite towns and cities of refuge
passages.summary: The law provides towns for Levites and refuge for people accused of killing. It distinguishes accidental death from intentional murder. The instructions require judgment about motive, witnesses, and circumstances. Refuge limits immediate retaliation while a case receives review.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how fair judgment requires more than an accusation. Read the ancient procedures within their legal setting.

passages.title: Inheritance and marriage
passages.summary: Leaders from Manasseh question the effects of the daughters’ inheritance. The daughters marry within their father’s tribe under the new instruction. The final chapter preserves the daughters’ inheritance while limiting its transfer between tribes. The protection comes with a restriction on marriage.
passages.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider both the protection and the limits in this legal decision. Keep its tribal setting distinct from present marriage choices.

events.title: Miriam dies, water flows, and Aaron dies

events.detail: The chapter records loss and leadership transition. Moses and Aaron also receive a judgment about entry into the land.
events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies meekness and trust. Read leadership duties alongside grief and the account’s limits on authority.

events.title: The bronze serpent and eastern victories
events.summary: The people suffer snakebites and receive a bronze serpent as a sign for healing. Israel then defeats Sihon and Og.
events.detail: The narrative combines complaint, healing, journeys, and war. Its victories do not establish a precise army route.
events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.title: Balak sends for Balaam

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: The Church lesson studies pressure to act against God’s will. Keep later comments about Balaam distinct from this chapter’s sequence.

events.title: Balaam blesses Israel
events.summary: Balak builds altars and seeks a curse. Balaam instead pronounces blessings. They move to another vantage point, but the result remains a blessing.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.title: A star and a scepter

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.title: Peor and Phinehas

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Read the manual’s priesthood discussion with care. Keep ancient narrative violence distinct from present religious duties.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a calendar can help a community remember its duties together.

events.title: Vows and household authority
events.summary: The laws regulate vows. Fathers and husbands can cancel certain vows made by women under the stated conditions.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider the responsibility of making promises. Do not transfer the ancient household rules directly into present relationships.

events.title: War against Midian
events.summary: Israel attacks Midian, and Balaam dies. Moses gives severe instructions about captives. The chapter also divides spoils and describes cleansing.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Read the entire chapter, including its violence. Keep this ancient war account distinct from present Church conduct.

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how a personal or group benefit can carry obligations to the wider community.

events.title: Borders and appointed leaders

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how clear duties can support a shared allocation. Keep expected borders distinct from verified historical control.

events.title: Levite towns and cities of refuge

events.uncertainty: Markers show regions or traditional identifications. Many campsites, the sea crossing, and Mount Hor lack secure locations.

lds.text: Consider how fair judgment requires more than an accusation. Read the ancient procedures within their legal setting.

guides.title: Study Numbers
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: The first census
steps.text: God commands a census of men eligible for war. Tribal leaders assist Moses and Aaron. Levites receive separate duties. The account presents a community organized for travel and service. Its totals are textual claims, not independently verified population counts.

steps.title: The red heifer and cleansing

The final chapter preserves the daughters’ inheritance while limiting its transfer between tribes. The protection comes with a restriction on marriage.
